records.initialClaim: Removing the termination-age check makes a stale, short-lived OOM grant quick-OOM eligibility and bypass ordinary update checks. Restore the requirement that now minus FinishedAt is strictly less than evictOOMThreshold.
records.initialEvidence: Removed: now.Sub(terminationState.Terminated.FinishedAt.Time) < evictOOMThreshold. Remaining condition: terminationState.Terminated.FinishedAt.Sub(terminationState.Terminated.StartedAt.Time) < evictOOMThreshold, followed by quickOOM = true. Ordinary checks are gated by: if !updatePriority.OutsideRecommendedRange && !quickOOM.
records.verificationExplanation: Removing the FinishedAt age check lets an old, short-lived OOM set quickOOM=true, bypassing pod-lifetime and minimum-change checks. The remaining ResourceDiff check only rejects zero changes, so stale OOMs can admit updates below MinChangePriority.
records.reason: Explains why the remaining zero-diff guard does not prevent nonzero updates below MinChangePriority.
records.justification: plausible, not established by recorded gate rationale

records.initialClaim: Cleanup is recorded as completed before collection runs, even when listing or deletion fails. Subsequent runs skip retrying until the GC interval elapses. Preserve error propagation and update lastCheckpointGC only after successful collection.
records.initialEvidence: MaintainCheckpoints: `r.lastCheckpointGC = time.Now()` precedes `r.clusterStateFeeder.GarbageCollectCheckpoints(ctx)`. The diff changes collection from returning `error` to returning nothing, replaces listing errors with `klog.ErrorS(err, "Cannot list VPAs"); return` and `klog.ErrorS(err, "Cannot list VPA checkpoints"); return`, and replaces aggregated deletion errors with logging.
records.verificationExplanation: The change replaces success-only timestamp updates with an unconditional update before collection. Failed collection attempts therefore suppress retries until the GC interval elapses, delaying cleanup.
records.reason: Ordering, error propagation and delayed retries were already present in the initial claim/evidence.
records.justification: plausible, not established by recorded gate rationale

records.initialClaim: Writing and garbage collection now share the writing deadline. If StoreCheckpoints exhausts that deadline, cleanup receives an expired context and cannot delete orphaned checkpoints. Restore separate timeout contexts created from the shared parent, starting the cleanup timeout when collection begins.
records.initialEvidence: RunOnce: `stepCtx, cancelFunc := context.WithDeadline(ctx, time.Now().Add(r.checkpointsWriteTimeout))`; `r.MaintainCheckpoints(stepCtx)`. MaintainCheckpoints: `r.checkpointWriter.StoreCheckpoints(ctx, r.updateWorkerCount)` followed by `r.clusterStateFeeder.GarbageCollectCheckpoints(ctx)`. The diff removes both independent timeout contexts.
records.verificationExplanation: The change passes one write-deadline context to both sequential operations. If writing exhausts that deadline, garbage collection starts with an expired context, whereas previously it received a fresh timeout from the parent. Cleanup can therefore be skipped, and advancing lastCheckpointGC delays another attempt.
records.reason: Repeats the expired deadline and links it to the timestamp effect already in the other finding.
records.justification: plausible, not established by recorded gate rationale

records.initialClaim: Using NumberReady reintroduces the documented recovery failure: a DaemonSet with five desired pods and zero ready pods now returns an error. Restore DesiredNumberScheduled and its zero-desired guard. The test change also removes the zero-ready regression case.
records.verificationExplanation: The change makes getReplicaCount return an error for a DaemonSet with five desired pods and zero ready pods; previously it returned 5. This directly confirms the reported replica-count regression, though the downstream recovery impact is not shown.
records.reason: Confirms local return/error behavior but explicitly leaves downstream recovery unsupported.
records.justification: plausible, not established by recorded gate rationale

records.initialClaim: The placeholder alternative lacks a start anchor, so malformed IDs such as junkaws:///us-east-1a/i-placeholder-some pass validation. Previously both alternatives required aws:/// at the beginning, as required by the note's invalid-format boundary.
records.initialEvidence:
New regex: `^aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/[-0-9a-z]*(\/[-0-9a-z\.]*)?$|aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/%s.*$`
Previous placeholder alternative: `^aws\:\/\/\/[-0-9a-z]*\/(%s.*)$`
Validation rejects only when validAwsRefIdRegex.FindStringSubmatch(id) == nil.
records.verificationExplanation: The placeholder alternative lost its leading ^, so FindStringSubmatch can match aws:/// after arbitrary leading text. Previously both alternatives were anchored. Such malformed IDs now pass validation and are parsed incorrectly because extraction still assumes aws:/// starts at offset zero.
records.reason: Adds the fixed-offset parsing consequence; target slash truncation remains missed.
records.justification: plausible, not established by recorded gate rationale
